newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends lower on spreads, soyoil slips.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends lower on spreads, soyoil slips.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended lower on Thursday, in line with losses in soybeans, on active unwinding of bull spreads, traders said.
Soyoil drew strength from strong weekly USDA export sales data but losses in soybeans overwhelmed the bullish input.
"We saw some big spread unwinding," said Brian Scott, vice president of R.J. O'Brien.

Uncertainty about the magnitude of a port strike in Brazil also weighed on the market. Soymeal rallied on Tuesday amid reports stevedores at Santos port were on strike and had called for a nationwide work stoppage on Friday.
But workers at Paranagua port had not yet decided whether to strike. Paranagua ships more soy products than Santos.
Concerns continued to circulate about dry weather in Brazil and Argentina cutting yields.

"If you go back about six weeks ago, the trade was pretty well expecting to have 45 million tonnes coming out of South America," said Doug Hjort, president of Hjort Associates. "Now I see some of the analysts from down there are saying there's probably not 27 million tonnes in Brazil."
Soymeal closed $3.40 per ton lower to $2.30 higher while soyoil ended down 0.30 to 0.05 cent per lb.
Weekly USDA export sales figures were supportive, but a mediocre soybean export figure outweighed strong soy product data, floor sources said.

USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soyoil during the week ended March 27 totaled 18,400 tonnes, above expectations for 5,000 to 8,000 tonnes. But soybean sales of 216,400 tonnes were disappointing. Traders had expected 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.

Unwinding of bull spreads was the featured play in soymeal. Traders said Merrill Lynch spread 50 lots August/July at $11 to $10.50 per ton, premium July, traders said. The July/December spread closed at $66.20, premium July.
On the day, E.D. and F. Man International bought 600 lots May soymeal, Prudential Securities bought 100 May and 400 July, and Refco Inc bought 100 July and 300 May, traders said.
In soyoil, ADM bought 400 lots May, Continental Grain and Tenco Inc each bought 200 May and ING sold 100 May and 200 July, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 19,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 26,712 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 14,000 lots, against Wednesday's 19,374 lots.
